The agreement governs the remarketing of Series E Senior Component Debentures. Key obligations include the appointment and duties of the Remarketing Agents, representations and warranties by the Company regarding securities laws compliance, covenants to prepare prospectuses and maintain qualifications, and indemnification provisions. There are no explicit termination clauses for convenience or standard breach with cure periods; termination is tied to the success of the remarketing or resignation/removal of agents. No governing law clause is present in this chunk. No renewal terms or fixed contract value are explicitly stated as a lump sum; fees are described as 'Remarketing Fee' to be specified in a Pricing Agreement.

This document is Chunk 2 of a Remarketing Agreement. It contains the tail end of Section 6 (Indemnification), Sections 7 through 22, signature pages, and several Annexes. Key obligations extracted include contribution limits for agents, resignation/removal procedures, offering restrictions, governing law, and survival clauses. The effective date is found in the Annex III letter as August 26, 2014.

Key obligations include detailing requirements, sales force maintenance, exclusivity regarding competing products, non-disparagement, employee solicitation restrictions, audit rights, and specific termination provisions for regulatory failure, breach, and performance. The term expires on March 31, 2020. Compensation is based on service fees tied to cumulative net sales exceeding a baseline and milestone payments.

It covers confidentiality exceptions, exclusivity, non-compete/non-disparagement restrictions, employee solicitation limits, intellectual property ownership and license grants, indemnification, liability caps, insurance, dispute resolution, miscellaneous provisions (assignment, governing law), and several exhibits detailing safety reporting, records management, compliance, and insurance. Key obligations include exclusivity in the territory, non-disparagement of the Product, no-solicit of employees, IP ownership by Janssen, limited license to use trademarks, anti-assignment restrictions, liability caps, and audit rights.

key_obligations: You receive a Designated Area within which we and our affiliates shall not operate or grant to anyone else a franchise to operate a Buffalo Wild Wings or bw-3 Restaurant so long as this Agreement is in force and effect.

You will not, at any time during or after the term of this Agreement, divulge to any person, partnership, corporation or any other entity any information, trade secrets, the ingredients, recipes, cooking techniques and processes, used in the Trade Secret Food Products, and other food and beverage products and Menu Items used in the System or any information stated in the Manuals.

You will not, at any time during or after the term of this Agreement, divulge to any person, partnership, corporation or any other entity any information, trade secrets, the ingredients, recipes, cooking techniques and processes, used in the Trade Secret Food Products

reasoning.summary:
The document is a Strategic Alliance Agreement between MD Anderson and Adaptimmune entities. Key obligations include funding commitments, study conduct responsibilities, IP ownership and licensing (including ROFR/ROFN), audit rights, insurance requirements, and non-assignment restrictions. The term is five years or until completion of studies. Termination includes for cause with cure periods, specific study termination rights, and a limited unilateral termination period for MD Anderson. Governing law is Texas.

The provided document is Chunk 2 of 2, consisting almost entirely of redacted pages (marked with '***' and confidentiality statements), a payment schedule table (Exhibit II), a Study Order template (Exhibit III), and a press release (Exhibit IV). The operative legal clauses (governing law, termination, key obligations, term length) are located in the main body of the Strategic Collaboration Agreement, which is not present in this chunk. Only the parties can be definitively identified from the Exhibit III preamble and Exhibit IV text. No other schema fields contain extractable operative language.

reasoning.summary: The document is a Sponsorship Agreement between National Processing Company (NPC) and National City Bank of Kentucky (NCB), dated June 30, 1996. The agreement establishes NPC as NCB's sole agent for merchant processing services. Key obligations include NPC's performance of services, compliance with Visa/MasterCard rules, indemnification of NCB, and specific restrictions on assignment. The term is five years with automatic one-year renewals unless notice of non-renewal is given six months prior. Termination can occur by mutual agreement, for breach (with cure periods), or upon bankruptcy/termination of NCB's bankcard membership. Governing law is US and Kentucky law.

reasoning.summary:
The document is a Collaboration Agreement between Theravance, Inc. and Glaxo Group Limited dated November 14, 2002. The agreement covers the development and commercialization of Long-Acting β2 Adrenoceptor Agonists. Key obligations include license grants, milestone payments, royalty payments on net sales, supply obligations, and specific restrictions on clinical development outside the collaboration. The term is defined by patent expiration or 15 years from first commercial sale. Termination rights exist for material breach, discontinuation of development, and commercialization. Governing law is not explicitly stated in this chunk.

This chunk (2 of 3) covers the financial, regulatory, supply, confidentiality, IP prosecution, and termination sections of a Collaboration Agreement between GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) and Theravance. Key obligations extracted include royalty payment mechanics, audit rights, insurance procurement, patent prosecution duties, and detailed post-termination wind-down provisions. The document name is inferred from the context as a 'Collaboration Agreement'.

This chunk (3 of 3) contains the closing sections of a Stock Purchase Agreement between Theravance, Inc. and Glaxo Group Limited (GSK). It includes stock purchase restrictions, voting rights, transfer restrictions, miscellaneous provisions (relationship of parties, force majeure, governing law, assignment, notices, severability, waiver, entire agreement, no license, third-party beneficiaries), a single closing condition with termination rights, and the signature block. Key obligations extracted include anti-assignment clauses, change of control definitions/impacts, third-party beneficiary disclaimers, and specific stock purchase/voting restrictions.

termination_clauses: Either Party may, without prejudice to any other remedies available to it at law or in equity, terminate this Agreement subject to Section 14.10 in the event that the other Party (as used in this subsection, the "Breaching Party") shall have materially breached or defaulted in the performance of any of its obligations. The Breaching Party shall, if such breach can be cured, have sixty (60) days after written notice thereof was provided to the Breaching Party by the non-breaching Party to remedy such default (or, if such default cannot be cured within such 60-day period, the Breaching Party must commence and diligently continue actions to cure such default during such 60-day period). Any such termination shall become effective at the end of such 60-day period unless the Breaching Party has cured any such breach or default prior to the expiration of such 60-day period (or, if such default is capable of being cured but cannot be cured within such 60-day period, the Breaching Party has commenced and diligently continued actions to cure such default provided always that, in such instance, such cure must have occurred within one hundred twenty (120) days after written notice thereof was provided to the Breaching Party by the non-breaching Party to remedy such default).

On a Collaboration Product-by-Collaboration Product basis, and at any time during Development and prior to First Commercial Sale of the applicable Collaboration Product, GSK shall have the right to terminate Development of such Collaboration Product (upon the provision of ninety (90) days written notice) for reasons of Technical Failure or Commercial Failure following communication to, and assessment of such proposed termination by, the Joint Project Committee and Joint Steering Committee (in which case such Collaboration Product shall be referred to as a "Terminated Development Collaboration Product").

On a Collaboration Product-by- Collaboration Product basis, and on a Country-by-Country basis, at any time after First Commercial Sale of the applicable Collaboration Product in such country, GSK shall have the right to terminate Commercialization of such Collaboration Product (upon the provision of one hundred and eighty (180) days written notice) for reasons of Commercial Failure or Technical Failure and following communication to, and assessment of such proposed termination by, the Joint Project Committee and Joint Steering Committee (in which case, such Collaboration Product shall be referred to as a "Terminated Commercialized Collaboration Product").

Any time following the third anniversary of the Effective Date, either Party may terminate this Agreement, subject to Section 14.10, upon the provision of ninety (90) days written notice if Development of all Collaboration Products and all Pooled Compounds have been discontinued for Technical Failure and/or Commercial Failure.

This Agreement may be terminated by either Party upon written notice any time after June 1, 2003 if the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall not have been consummated by June 1, 2003 due to failure to satisfy the Closing Condition; provided, however, that the terminating Party shall not have breached in any material respect its obligations under this Agreement in any manner that shall have been the proximate cause of, or resulted in, the failure to satisfy the Closing Condition or otherwise to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement by such date.

reasoning.summary: The document is a Marketing and Transportation Services Agreement between Purolator Courier Ltd. and Parcelway Courier Systems Canada Ltd. (Dynamex), dated November 20, 1995. The agreement establishes a cooperative marketing and service provision arrangement. Key obligations include exclusive tendering of specific service types (sameday vs overnight/next day), non-solicitation of each other's customers for competing services, insurance maintenance, indemnification, and performance standards. Termination provisions include termination for cause with notice periods and termination without cause with a two-year notice period. There is no fixed term; it continues indefinitely until terminated.

reasoning.summary: The document is a License and Reseller Agreement between Ehave, Inc. and Companion Healthcare Technologies Corp., dated October 30, 2018. The agreement grants CHT an exclusive license to resell the Ehave Companion Solution in the Territory for the Field of Use. Key obligations include royalty payments (Schedule 6), development milestones, marketing duties, and confidentiality. The term is perpetual. Termination rights exist for cause (breach, insolvency) and convenience (with fee). Governing law is Ontario. Liability is capped at 12 months of fees. Insurance requirements are specified.

entries.evidence: THIS LICENSE AND RESELLER AGREEMENT
Ehave, Inc. ('Ehave'); Companion Healthcare Technologies Corp ('CHT')
October 30, 2018

This term of this Agreement and the rights and obligations of the Parties hereto shall commence as of the Effective Date and shall continue in perpetuity (the 'Term'), unless terminated earlier in accordance with the provisions contained herein.

Subject to Sections 10(e) and 10(g), CHT may terminate this Agreement and the rights granted hereunder, in whole or in part... immediately upon giving written notice of such termination if Ehave: (i) breaches any material provision of this Agreement and such breach continues for a period of twenty (20) Business Days after delivery of a written notice by CHT requiring Ehave to correct such failure; or (ii) becomes or is adjudicated insolvent or bankrupt...

In addition, CHT may terminate this Agreement and the rights granted hereunder, in whole or in part... at any time without cause, by providing at least thirty (30) Business Days prior written notice to Ehave, but subject to payment of a termination fee equal to an amount set out in Schedule 6.

Subject to Sections 10(e) and 10(g), Ehave may terminate this Agreement and the rights granted hereunder without prejudice to enforcement of any other legal right or remedy, immediately upon giving written notice of such termination if CHT: (i) fails to pay in full any sum owing by it under this Agreement by the due date thereof... and such failure continues for a period of ten (10) Business Days after delivery of a written notice by Ehave requiring CHT to correct such failure; (ii) breaches any other material provision of this Agreement and such breach continues for a period of twenty (20) Business Days after delivery of a written notice by Ehave requiring CHT to correct such failure;

This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws in force in the Province of Ontario (excluding any conflict of laws rule or principle which might refer such construction to the laws of another jurisdiction).

Subject to Section 2(e), the foregoing appointment is exclusive such that Ehave shall not appoint any other Person to, nor may Ehave itself, sell or resell the use of the Ehave Companion Solution within the Field of Use anywhere in the Territory.

Ehave hereby grants to CHT a non-transferable (except as permitted under Section 20(f)), right to: (i) sub-license the use of the Ehave Companion Solution within the Field of Use in the Territory to End Users and their respective Authorized Users

Confidential information has been redacted in several places, affecting the extraction of specific monetary values and some exclusivity details.

reasoning.summary: The document is a Joint Venture Agreement between Novo Integrated Sciences Inc. (NVOS) and Harvest Gold Farms Inc. (HGF), dated December 19, 2019. The agreement outlines the development of hemp and medicinal crops. Key obligations include NVOS's duties to maintain records, direct operations, remunerate HGF, and purchase product at cost plus 5%, as well as HGF's duties to provide land (minimum 7,000 acres), assist in marketing, and grow crops to high standards. The term is five years with renewal options. Assignment rights are unilateral for NVOS (notice only) and conditional for HGF (consent required). There is no explicit governing law clause, uncapped liability, or insurance requirement found in the text.

reasoning.summary: The document is an AIRSOPURE Franchise Agreement (Exhibit C) entered into in 2000 between Airsopure International Group, Inc. and a Franchisee ('You'). The agreement grants an exclusive franchise for air cleaning systems. Key obligations include payment of initial fees, royalties (5% of gross sales), advertising fees (2%), and local advertising spend. It contains strict exclusivity provisions regarding the territory and customer solicitation, non-compete covenants during the term and for two years post-termination within a 25-mile radius, and non-solicit restrictions on employees and customers. Transfer rights are heavily restricted with a Right of First Refusal held by AIRSOPURE. Insurance requirements are specified. Termination clauses cover immediate termination for cause (insolvency, fraud, etc.) and termination for default with a 30-day cure period. The governing law is Texas.

reasoning.summary:
The document is a Network Build and Maintenance Agreement between Commnet Wireless, LLC (Vendor) and AT&T Mobility LLC. The text provided covers the preamble, scope, definitions, and general terms including assignment, indemnity, IP, insurance, and limitation of liability. Key family clauses identified include Anti-Assignment restrictions, Change of Control definitions and termination rights, License Grants for IP, Audit Rights, Insurance requirements, Limitation of Damages (Cap on Liability), and Governing Law.

This chunk (2 of 3) contains the core operative provisions of a Master Services Agreement between AT&T Mobility LLC and Commnet Wireless, LLC. It covers indemnification, insurance, payment terms, IP ownership/licensing, limitation of damages, audit rights, termination, and various covenants. Key obligations include maintaining specific insurance coverages, assigning IP to AT&T, granting perpetual licenses, providing audit access, and adhering to strict termination and non-compete-like market restrictions.

This chunk (3 of 3) contains the closing sections of a Master Services Agreement between AT&T Mobility LLC/AT&T Services, Inc. and Commnet Wireless, LLC. It includes detailed operational covenants regarding Customer Information security, access control, background checks, hazardous materials, independent contractor status, liens, safety, data ownership (AT&T Data/Derived Data), FOSS compliance, and dispute resolution. The signature block confirms the parties and effective date.
